915:
(a) Eligibility to file an appeal. Only applicants or feepayors who have already been assessed an impact fee by the county or who have already received a written determination of refund or credit amount shall be entitled to an appeal.
(b) Appeals process.
(1) The aggrieved applicant or feepayor must file a written appeal with the administrator within fifteen (15) days of the receipt of written determination of the amount of the development impact fee due, or entitlement to an amount of a refund or credit. Such written appeal shall be of sufficient content to clearly and unequivocally set forth the basis for the appeal and the relief sought.
(2) Such written appeal shall state the basis for the appeal and the relief sought, and shall include:
1. The name and address of the aggrieved applicant or feepayor;
2. The location of the affected property; and
3. A copy of any applicable written decision or determination made by the administrator from which the appeal is taken.
(3) Within fifteen (15) days after receipt of the appeal, the administrator shall make a written decision with respect to the appeal. Such decision shall be of sufficient content to set forth the basis for the determination.
(4) Appeals from the decision of the administrator shall be made to the board of commissioners within thirty (30) days of receipt of the administrator's decision by the aggrieved applicant or feepayor. Delivery by hand or certified mail to, or posting upon the property, at the address given by the aggrieved applicant or feepayor in the application for relief shall constitute "receipt by the aggrieved applicant or feepayor" under this provision.
(5) The board of commissioners shall thereafter establish a reasonable date and time for a hearing on the appeal, give written notice thereof to the applicant or feepayor in the same manner as provided in subsection 8-6012(b)(4), and decide the issue within thirty (30) days following the hearing. Any party making an appeal shall have the right to appear at the hearing to present evidence and may be represented by counsel.
(c) Payment of impact fee during appeal.
(1) The filing of an appeal shall not stay the collection of a development impact fee as a condition to the issuance of development approval.
(2) A developer may pay a development impact fee under protest to obtain a development approval, and by making such payment shall not be stopped from exercising this right of appeal or receiving a refund of any amount deemed to have been collected in excess.

916:
(a) Enforcement authority.
(1) The enforcement of the ordinance shall be the responsibility of the administrator and such personnel as the administrator may designate from time to time.
(2) The administrator shall have the right to inspect the lands affected by the ordinance and shall have the right to issue cease and desist orders and citations for violations. Refusal of written notice of violation under the ordinance shall constitute legal notice of service.
(3) The administrator may suspend any building permit or withhold the issuance of other development approvals if the provisions of the ordinance have been violated by the developer or the owner or their assigns.
(4) For any violation, the administrator shall have the authority to issue a citation. The citation shall be in the form of a written official notice issued in person or by certified mail to the owner of the property, or to his or her agent, or to the person performing the work. The receipt of a citation shall require that corrective action be taken within thirty (30) days unless otherwise extended at the discretion of the administrator. If the required corrective action is not taken within the time allowed, the administrator may use any available civil or criminal remedies to secure compliance, including revoking a permit.
(b) Violations.
(1) Knowingly furnishing false information on any matter relating to the administration of the ordinance shall constitute an actionable violation.
(2) Proceeding with construction of a project that is not consistent with the project's impact fee assessment, such as the use category claimed or units of development indicated, shall constitute an actionable violation.
(3) Failure to take corrective action following the receipt of a citation shall constitute an actionable violation.
(4) A violation of the ordinance shall be a misdemeanor punishable according to law. However, in addition to or in lieu of criminal prosecution, the board of commissioners shall have the power to sue in law or equity for relief in civil court to enforce the ordinance, including recourse to such civil and criminal remedies in law and equity as may be necessary to ensure compliance with the provisions of the ordinance, including, but not limited to, injunctive relief to enjoin and restrain any person from violating the provisions of the ordinance and to recover such damages as may be incurred by the implementation of specific corrective actions.
(Res. No. 2023-RES-009, 5-1-23)
917:
(a) Repeal of conflicting laws. Any and all ordinances, resolutions, or regulations, or parts thereof, in conflict with the ordinance are hereby repealed to the extent of such conflict.
(b) Severability. If any sentence, clause, part, paragraph, section, or provision of the ordinance is declared by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, the validity of the ordinance as a whole or any other part hereof shall not be affected.
(c) Incorporation by reference of Georgia law. It is the intent of the board of commissioners that the development impact fee ordinance of Spalding County comply with the terms and provisions of the Georgia Development Impact Fee Act (O.C.G.A. §§ 36-71-1 et seq. as amended). Therefore, said chapter 36-71 of the Official Code of Georgia is incorporated by reference into the ordinance. To the extent that any provision of the ordinance is inconsistent with the provisions of said Title 36, Chapter 71, the latter shall control. Furthermore, to the extent that the ordinance is silent as to any provision of said Title 36 Chapter 71 that is otherwise deemed mandatory by law, such provision shall control and shall be binding upon the county.
(d) Effective date.
(1) The ordinance shall take effect upon June 1, 2023.
(2) Any building for which a valid building permit has been issued prior to the effective date of the ordinance may proceed without payment of additional impact fees otherwise imposed by the ordinance in accordance with the provisions of subsection 8-6004(c) regarding grandfathered projects.

(a) General.
(1) Applications must be verified before final approvals are given. Approval will be in writing with copies to all interested parties.
(2) Indigent cases, except emergencies, must be approved before admission to hospital. There will be no retroactive approvals except emergencies.
(3) Emergency cases must be reported to approving agent within twenty-four (24) hours after admission to the hospital if they are considered for approval as indigent, except when emergency cases enter the hospital on a Saturday or a Sunday. Such Saturday or Sunday cases must be submitted to the approving agent for investigation by 9:00 a.m. on the following Tuesday.
(4) Except in the case of approvals for "outpatient" treatment, each hospital admission as an indigent will require a separate application and approval.
(5) An "indigent" person as used herein shall be construed to mean any person, residing in Spalding County, who is ill or injured and is in need of hospital care and who from his own resources or from the resources of those upon whom he is legally dependent, is financially unable to meet the full costs of hospital care as prescribed or ordered by a physician. An allegedly indigent person shall not be considered "indigent" hereunder if any of the following conditions exist:
a. If either he or a person upon whom he is legally dependent is financially able to pay for his hospital care and, in any case, only to the extent of such hospital care for which he or those upon whom he is legally dependent are unable to pay;
b. If he or any one (1) or more of those upon whom he is legally dependent own a home or have an equity in a home, exceeding twenty-five hundred dollars ($2,500.00);
c. If he owns a motor vehicle or an equity therein which has a market value in excess of five hundred dollars ($500.00); or
d. If he has a stereo-record player, a television set, a motorcycle, an airplane, or other such items, which may be considered nonessential by the governing authority of Spalding County, having a market value in aggregate in excess of five hundred dollars ($500.00) or if he is making installment payments for the purchase of any such items.
(b) Insurance.
(1) No portion of any hospital bill for hospital care furnished anyone shall be regarded as an indigent case to the extent covered by any type of insurance or any federal, state, or other local programs for such indigent person.
(2) The term "hospital care" as used herein shall be construed to mean only the nonprofit, basic costs of hospital care needed for the treatment for the ill or injured, as deemed necessary and ordered by the physician in charge of the case in accordance with the rules, regulations and standards adopted and promulgated by the hospital, and shall be only the hospital care that is not available under any other program, federal, state or local.
(c) Pregnancy.
(1) As a general rule, pregnancy or childbirth will not be approved as an indigent case because there is ample time to make some arrangements to handle the financial obligation. If such a patient is clearly to be an indigent case, it must be reported by the doctor, patient or health clinic at least three (3) months in advance or as soon as the initial contact is made between the patient and the doctor or health clinic.
(2) No illegitimate pregnancy or childbirth will be approved as indigent unless the doctor, health clinic and/or the hospital notifies the approving agent in strict accordance with the above paragraph (1); and, further, that cooperation is extended to bring the putative father to justice by making him face his financial obligation under the law, and that the expectant mother swears out a warrant against the man she names as the father of the child. The county investigator should be called for assistance in these cases.
(d) Doctors. Spalding County assumes no liability for physicians' bills or hospital resident physicians' fees.
